texts.error.bad_clock: CPU Clock (MHz) is %1: it is 0 for the CPU's own clock, or 1 to 2000.
texts.error.cpu_not_taken: This machine does not take a '%1'. It takes: %2
texts.error.no_blit: There is no room for the picture's bitmap.
texts.error.no_frame_buffer: There is no room for the frame buffer.
texts.error.no_save_window: There is no room for the save data window.
texts.error.pci_timing: The PCI bus's timing came out as %1 and %2 CPU cycles at this clock.
texts.firmware.device_rom.about: The ROM of the %1, which you supply.
texts.firmware.machine_rom.about: A ROM of the %1, which you supply. PCem ships no ROMs.
texts.firmware.mda_rom.about: The 8x8 and 8x14 character shapes that an MDA or CGA-type card draws text with. Without it the machine starts with a blank screen. PCem loads fonts without reporting a missing one.
texts.firmware.video_bios.about: The video BIOS of the %1, which you supply.
texts.preset.dos_early_90s.about: A Pentium 133 with the Cirrus Logic video on its motherboard and a Sound Blaster 16, for DOS games released from 1990 to 1994.
texts.preset.dos_late_80s.about: A 20 MHz 386DX with VGA and a Sound Blaster Pro v2, for DOS games released up to the end of 1989.
texts.preset.dos_late_90s.about: A Pentium II/450 with an S3 Trio64 and a separate Voodoo Graphics card beside it, for DOS games released from 1995 on.
texts.preset.win95b_osr2.about: A Pentium II/233 with 256 MB of memory and a Voodoo 3 3000. TASVideos installs Windows 95 OSR 2 on this machine.
texts.preset.winxp_sp3_home: Windows XP SP3 Home Edition - Gigabyte GA-686BX
texts.preset.winxp_sp3_home.about: A Pentium II/450 with 256 MB of memory, a Voodoo 3 3000 and an AWE32. TASVideos installs Windows XP on this machine.
texts.setting.awe32emuaddress.about: The I/O port address of the EMU8000 wavetable chip on the Sound Blaster AWE32. Only the AWE32 has one.
texts.setting.awe32onboardram.about: How much sample memory the Sound Blaster AWE32 has. Only the AWE32 has any.
texts.setting.bpbdisable.about: Ignores the BIOS Parameter Block in the boot sector when working out a floppy disk's format. A few copy-protected disks need this.
texts.setting.cdchannel.about: Which IDE position the CD-ROM drive has: 0 is primary master, 1 primary slave, 2 secondary master and 3 secondary slave. PCs of the time had it at 2. The TASVideos late-1990s configuration uses 3, so that both hard disks can have the primary channel to themselves.
texts.setting.cddrive.about: Whether the machine has a CD-ROM drive. 'Auto' adds one when the project has a disc for the CD-ROM drive and leaves it out when it has none, which is what almost everyone wants. 'Fitted' gives the machine an empty drive, so software that looks for a drive finds one. 'None' never adds one.
texts.setting.cdmodel.about: Which drive model the machine reports that it has.
texts.setting.cdspeed.about: The drive's speed multiplier. It changes how long a read takes, so it is part of the machine.
texts.setting.cpu.about: The processor, by name. The list has every processor PCem knows. Each machine accepts only some of them. One that the machine does not accept is refused when the project loads, with a list of those it does accept. The manufacturer follows from the name, so there is nothing else to choose.
texts.setting.cpuclockmhz.about: 0 means the chosen processor's own clock speed. Any other value runs that processor at this speed instead, faster or slower. The chip and its timings stay as chosen, and only its speed changes. So a Pentium II/450 at 900 is a Pentium II twice as fast, which PCem has no entry for. 2000 is the most PCem's timers can hold. A faster machine takes proportionally more work to emulate.
texts.setting.cpuwaitstates.about: Memory wait states, for the machines where PCem models them. 0 is the machine's own default.
texts.setting.driveatype.about: The physical drive in bay A. 'Auto' chooses the drive that fits the image given for this drive, by the image's size. An image of 360k or smaller gets a 5.25" 360k drive, 720k a 3.5" 720k drive, 1.2M a 5.25" 1.2M drive, 1.44M a 3.5" 1.44M drive and 2.88M a 3.5" 2.88M drive. With no image, or with an image whose size is not a standard format (an .fdi, .td0, .imd or .86f file contains its own geometry), Auto chooses a 3.5" 1.44M drive, the most common one. A drive chosen by name is always used. The drive really matters: PCem does not refuse a disk that the drive cannot read completely. It stops the head at the drive's last track, and the machine gets read errors.
texts.setting.drivebtype.about: The physical drive in bay B. It works the same way as Floppy Drive A. With nothing in bay B, Auto chooses a 5.25" 1.2M drive, the second drive a PC of the time usually had.
texts.setting.dynarec.about: PCem's dynamic recompiler. It is much faster than the interpreter on a 486 and later. Its results are NOT exactly the same as the interpreter's, because the two calculate floating point differently. So it is part of the machine, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.fpsnumerator.about: How much time of the emulated PC one frame is. 100/1 means a frame is 10 ms, which is what every published PCem movie uses. It is part of the movie: the same inputs at a different rate give a different run.
texts.setting.fpu.about: A maths coprocessor (FPU). 'builtin' is for a 486DX and later, where it is part of the processor. 8087, 287, 287XL and 387 are the separate chips that an 8088, a 286 and a 386 could take. 'none' is for a machine sold without one. A processor with a built-in coprocessor always has it, whatever is chosen here. If the processor cannot take the chosen chip, that processor's own first choice is used.
texts.setting.gameblaster.about: A Creative Game Blaster (CMS), in addition to the card above.
texts.setting.gus.about: A Gravis Ultrasound, in addition to the card above.
texts.setting.hdd2cylinders.about: Cylinders of the second hard disk.
texts.setting.hdd2heads.about: Heads of the second hard disk.
texts.setting.hdd2sectors.about: Sectors per track of the second hard disk.
texts.setting.hddcontroller.about: The disk controller: MFM, ESDI, IDE, XT-IDE or SCSI. A machine with IDE on its motherboard does not need one here.
texts.setting.hddcylinders.about: Cylinders of the image in the hard disk slot.
texts.setting.hddgeometry.about: 'Auto' reads the disk's cylinders, heads and sectors from the image itself. It first uses the values in the image's own partition table, and then the image's length. This is right for any image made by PCem, DOS, Windows or this core. A .vhd file contains its geometry, and that is always used. 'Custom' shows the three numbers, for an image without partitions whose size is not a whole number of cylinders. A wrong geometry gives a disk that does not start, not an error message, so prefer Auto.
texts.setting.hddheads.about: Heads of the image in the hard disk slot.
texts.setting.hddsectors.about: Sectors per track of the image in the hard disk slot.
texts.setting.joysticktype.about: What is plugged into the game port.
texts.setting.lpt1device.about: What is plugged into the first parallel port (LPT1): nothing, a Covox-style sound adapter (DAC), or a Disney Sound Source.
texts.setting.machine.about: Which PC this is: the motherboard, its BIOS, its chipset and the processors it accepts. There are %1 machines, from a 1981 IBM PC to a Slot 1 Pentium II board. It decides which BIOS ROM the project asks you for.
texts.setting.memsizekb.about: The memory (RAM) in kilobytes. Every machine has its own minimum, maximum and step size, and the value is limited to them exactly as PCem does it. For example an IBM AT takes at most 16 MB and a GA-686BX at most 512 MB.
texts.setting.mousesensitivity.about: Every relative mouse movement is multiplied by this number before the machine receives it. The unit is the mickey, the mouse's own step of movement. It applies to Mouse X/Y and to the movement that Mouse Position X/Y causes. It changes how far the mouse has to travel, not where the pointer ends: an absolute position still lands where it says, but it takes this many times as many steps to get there. It is the same setting, with the same default, as in the DOSBox-X core.
texts.setting.mousetype.about: Which mouse is plugged in. A machine with no PS/2 port needs a serial mouse. The Amstrad and Olivetti mice are built into those machines.
texts.setting.oplemulator.about: Which emulation of the Yamaha OPL chip the card's FM sound uses. NukedOPL is the accurate one, and the TASVideos PCem configurations use it. DBOPL is faster. They do not sound the same and do not behave the same, so it is part of the machine, and a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.soundcard.about: The sound card in the machine.
texts.setting.soundcardaddress.about: The I/O port address of the sound card. 0x220 is where PCs of the time had a Sound Blaster, and almost every DOS game assumes it. 'Card default' leaves the address the chosen card was sold with. An address the chosen card cannot have is ignored.
texts.setting.soundcarddma.about: The DMA channel the sound card uses, on the cards that let you choose it.
texts.setting.soundcardirq.about: The interrupt line (IRQ) the sound card uses. Only the older Sound Blasters let you choose it. A Sound Blaster 16 and later read it from their own configuration.
texts.setting.ssi2001.about: An Innovation SSI-2001, the PC card that carries the Commodore 64's SID sound chip.
texts.setting.system.about: This core emulates one kind of system: an IBM-compatible x86 PC. Which PC it is (the motherboard and its BIOS) is chosen with the Machine setting below. Every other part is chosen separately.
texts.setting.videobilinear.about: Bilinear texture filtering, on the 3D cards that have it (a Voodoo Banshee or Voodoo 3). It changes the picture, so it is part of the machine.
texts.setting.videocard.about: The graphics card. 'builtin' uses the video hardware on the machine's own motherboard, where it has any. The list has every card PCem emulates, from MDA to a Voodoo 3. All of them are emulated in software.
texts.setting.videomemory.about: How much memory the graphics card has. It decides which video modes the card can show. Each card offers its own sizes: a Trio64 has 1, 2 or 4 MB, and an AVGA2 has 256 or 512 kB. A size the chosen card does not offer is ignored, so 'Card default' is always safe.
texts.setting.videorecompiler.about: The 3dfx cards' own recompiler for drawing pixels.
texts.setting.videorenderthreads.about: How many slices the 3dfx cards split a triangle into. In this build they are slices and not threads: the TASVideos version of PCem draws them one after another, in order. The split still changes what is drawn and how the texture cache behaves, so it is part of the machine. The TASVideos configurations use 1.
texts.setting.videoscreenfilter.about: The output filter of the 3dfx cards. It blurs the picture the way the real card's output stage did.
texts.setting.videospeed.about: How fast the card's bus is. 'default' leaves it to the card.
texts.setting.voodoo.about: A 3dfx Voodoo Graphics or Voodoo 2 as a SEPARATE card added beside the 2D card above, which is how they were sold.
texts.setting.voodoobilinear.about: Bilinear texture filtering on the added Voodoo card.
texts.setting.voodooframebuffermemory.about: The framebuffer memory of the added Voodoo card. It decides which resolutions the card can show.
texts.setting.voodoorecompiler.about: The added Voodoo card's own recompiler for drawing pixels.
texts.setting.voodoorenderthreads.about: How many slices the added Voodoo card splits a triangle into. See Video Render Threads.
texts.setting.voodooscreenfilter.about: The output filter of the added Voodoo card.
texts.setting.voodoosli.about: Two Voodoo cards working together (SLI), each drawing half of the lines. A pair of Voodoo 2 cards was sold this way.
texts.setting.voodootexturememory.about: The texture memory of the added Voodoo card, for each texture unit (TMU).
texts.setting.voodootype.about: Which 3dfx card the Voodoo Graphics setting above adds.
texts.slot.cdrom.help: Discs for the CD-ROM drive. PCem reads the image itself, so a .cue file with its track files beside it works. It needs a machine with a CD-ROM controller. The CD-ROM settings appear once a disc is given here.
texts.slot.floppy_a.help: Disk images for drive A:. The first is in the drive when the machine starts, and the order here is the order they are swapped in. The drive itself is chosen with the Floppy Drive A setting. Its default is Auto, which chooses the drive that fits the image you give here. If you choose a drive yourself, make sure it matches. PCem does not refuse a disk that the drive cannot read completely. It stops the head at the drive's last track, and the machine gets read errors.
texts.slot.floppy_b.help: Disk images for drive B:. It works the same way as drive A:. A machine with only one drive ignores this.
texts.slot.hdd.help: A hard disk image, used as drive C:. Your file is never changed. The machine works on a copy of it that can be written to. What is written stays for the session, is part of savestates, and can be exported as save data. An exported image can be given here to continue from it. The disk's geometry is worked out from the file unless the Hard Disk settings say otherwise.
texts.slot.hdd2.help: A second hard disk. It works the same way.
